### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via permissionSets (literal, a string literal in actions))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via list_toolbar (literal, a string literal in actions))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 54 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5271c3f48ae33dd679fdd56e9fbec6065e153ab` — the merge of head `2469b6cee764dd2a1202dc56166085d0b7e47361` into base `12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b5271c3f48ae33dd679fdd56e9fbec6065e153ab && git checkout b5271c3f48ae33dd679fdd56e9fbec6065e153ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70 2469b6cee764dd2a1202dc56166085d0b7e47361 && git checkout -B drift-repro 12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70 && git merge --no-ff 2469b6cee764dd2a1202dc56166085d0b7e47361

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 12a0f09fca49bf90747e9cea21d566229c33de70` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5f0e9b5f73df47f63416f08094fb06b8a8372aeb`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. `reviewFace` decides no face from the 28 paths; the committed changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line routes the review here. Inputs read: card #33186 (body, triage 6868765295, claim 6891528063, os-dev-report 6892329704), the PR #33755 body, its file list (28 files), the net diff against `main` (merge base `ee627c67`), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read to judge it, not reviewed.

Check-runs on `5f0e9b5f` at 2026-11-15T09:32Z: 12 success (Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, Check PR Size, Flag docs, Auto Label, filter), 16 skipped by path filter, 0 failed, and 20 still **in progress**: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, CI release and engine gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, query-options erasure, slot lookup and corpus), Live E2E UI. This verdict covers the contract only. Those gates answer for themselves, and the merge waits for them to go green. The dev's local runs were at `e6eb15eb`. The one later commit, `5f0e9b5f`, is a whitespace-only fix to `TEMPORARY_PASSWORD_LABEL` in `sys-user.object.ts:76` that puts back `main`'s spelling. It is not in the net diff, so the CI runs on this head are the ones that count.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/platform-objects` `SysUser.actions`: adds `add_sso_user` and `import_sso_users`.** This is right. It widens the surface and removes nothing. No existing action's `visible`, `requiresFeature` or params changed, and the diff touches no other member (`sys-user.object.ts:447-560`).
- **Visibility predicate `MANAGED_ADD_PERSON_VISIBLE` (`sys-user.object.ts:73-74`): `current_user.isPlatformAdmin == true && has(features.cloudManaged) && features.cloudManaged == true`.** This is right. It matches the answer domain of both doors. Each door answers 409 off a managed environment (`plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts:514`, read on `main`) and admits only the platform-admin standing (ADR-0068 D4). The `has()` guard stops the predicate faulting while no flag is served (a faulting action predicate SHOWS the action), which is the same trap `create_user`'s second email param guards. The pins in `cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts` check four things: the action is offered when managed, hidden when the flag is off, hidden rather than faulted when no flag is served, and hidden from an organization owner. They also pin the exact set of actions offered in each mode.
- **`requiredPermissions: [...PLATFORM_ADMIN_USERS_GATE]` (`sys-user.object.ts:456`, `:515`), with no `requiresFeature`.** This is right. `PLATFORM_ADMIN_USERS_GATE` is `['manage_users']` (`platform-admin-action-gate.ts:37`), which matches the changeset text and the family's other doors. The doors mount without the better-auth admin plugin (#33227), so `requiresFeature: 'admin'` would hide them on Free and Team kernels. Leaving it off is correct, and a test pins it.
- **Metadata accept-set: no change.** This is right. Every key the new actions use is already accepted on `main`: param `widget` (`spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:280`, an open string, with `position-ref` and `permission-ref` registered in the console), param `type` `email` / `textarea` / `text`, `resultDialog.fields[].format` `text` / `json` (`action.zod.ts:839`), `locations`, `refreshAfter`, and a CEL `visible`. No spec file is in the diff, which keeps to the claim's "⛔ No spec".
- **Door accept-set (closed body keys).** This is right. The `add_sso_user` param names `email`, `name`, `positions`, `permissionSets` and `manager` are exactly `ADD_KEYS` (`pending-sso-users.ts:185`). `import_sso_users` sends `{ csv }`, which is in `IMPORT_BODY_KEYS` (`pending-sso-users.ts:552`). A blank optional (`''` / `null`) is read as none (`pending-sso-users.ts:191`, `:217`). The live pins in `plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.test.ts` post the DECLARED action's dialog body to its `target`. On a managed boot, add returns 201 and import returns 200. The CONTROL boot returns 409 and adds nobody.
- **Result dialogs.** These are right on paths. `email`, `notApplied`, `managerError`, `host.reason`, `summary.*` and `rows` are all keys of the doors' answers (`pending-sso-users.ts:531-548`), and the dialog skips any path missing from the answer. One non-blocking should-fix (it affects neither correctness nor the contract): `.changeset/33186-managed-add-people-actions.md:10` says the Add User result "names an address that was already pending". That holds only when `notApplied` is non-empty. If someone re-adds an address that is still pending and sends no position, permission set or manager, the door returns 200 with `alreadyPending: true`, but the dialog (`sys-user.object.ts:490-502`) shows only "User Added" and the email. Either show `alreadyPending` or narrow that changelog sentence. #33187, which owns the follow-on UI, can carry this.
- **Translation surface: 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles plus 10 `*.source-hashes.generated.ts`.** This is right. New keys only, under `sys_user._actions.add_sso_user.*` / `import_sso_users.*`, with the `en` text identical to the declarations. The source-hash rows record values that the translated text leaves the same as the source (`CSV`, and German `Position`). `check:i18n` runs in the in-progress Lint jobs.
- **AI exposure: no `ai` block.** This is right. The actions stay human-only until someone assesses them under ADR-0011, as `list_platform_admins` does.
- **Test-guard changes.** These are right. `feature-gate-guard.test.ts:188-191` (`SHOWN_WHEN_ON`) relaxes the reverse walk only for an exact path and flag pair (`:277-278`). A new `describe` (`:282`) then holds each pair to the inverse conjuncts, on a `hide-when-on` flag, and checks the input is not booked the other way, so it opens no general bypass. `platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts:183-217` (`MODES`) now counts an action as offered when either mode offers it. That loosens only the "offered" direction for flag-dependent members, and the exact per-mode sets in `cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts` close the gap. The "refused principal" direction got stricter: it now holds in both modes. Byte rows in `platform-objects.test.ts` pin the two predicates exactly as served.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

- The changeset is `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch`. The PR body and the changeset body each carry the line-initial pair `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the two pairs agree.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct. Nothing a metadata author can write changed: no new key, value or type, and no spec path. Under the AGENTS.md post-task rule 3, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`, so the level matches what the diff publishes.
- The only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/platform-objects`. The `plugin-auth` change is a test file and publishes nothing, so no `plugin-auth` entry is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. Two actions and their locale keys are added, and nothing that was offered before is hidden or refused. The PR body's measurement table shows the six #25309 doors unchanged in both modes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], the test-local `SHOWN_WHEN_ON` ledger versus a new `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` member: answered A for this PR.** The claim's file surface rules out any spec change ("⛔ No spec"), the registry has no runtime reader, and the ledger is keyed by path and flag and held by its own `describe`. Whether the registry should ever model the show-when-on polarity is not owed by #33186. If the seat wants B, it becomes its own spec card with its own contract review. That does not block this PR.
- **open_questions[1], dropping `requiresFeature: 'admin'` from `sys_user.ban_user` / `unban_user`: answered A, its own card.** That change concerns deactivation, not adding, and it would widen ban and unban on every kernel without the admin plugin, managed or not. It needs its own measurement and its own `Clause-②` line. The seat files it under `domain:ui`, and this PR stays as it is.
- **Deviation, file surface.** Accepted. The claim names `sys-user.object.ts`, "their tests" and `.changeset/`. The extra paths are the 21 generated translation bundles (`check:i18n` requires them for any new label) and three test files (`plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.test.ts`, `feature-gate-guard.test.ts`, `platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts`). Those tests pin or admit the two new actions, and none of them is runtime code. The diff touches no other identity object and not `packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts`, which is consistent with the measurement.
- **Deviation, commit attribution trailer.** No contract effect, and nothing to rule here.
- **Out-of-scope finding (class a): on a managed environment, `sys_invitation.resend_invitation` is offered although `organization/invite-member` answers 409 there.** Escalated to the seat to file as its own `domain:ui` card. It is not an add-person action and is outside #33186's scope, and this PR correctly leaves that predicate unchanged.
- **Out-of-scope finding (carrier #33187): the per-row import UI.** It stays with #33187, which follows on the same branch. The should-fix in ① can travel with it.
- `security_findings: none`. The new actions add no privilege, because each door still applies its own platform-admin gate and returns 409 off a managed environment.
